issues.description: The solution implementation uses a different property name for the course instructor ('lecturer') than the problem statement and template ('instructor'). This name mismatch appears in the solution's Course class (property 'lecturer') while other code in the solution (Developer.attend) expects Course.instructor. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended property name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the course instructor property name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the Course property in the solution from 'lecturer' to 'instructor' (and adjust the initializer parameter) to match the problem statement and template, or change all references to use 'lecturer' and update the problem statement/template accordingly. Ensure Developer.attend and any other code access the same property name.

issues.description: The concept of the course teacher is referred to with two different identifiers: the problem statement and the template use the property/parameter name 'instructor', while the solution's Course implementation uses 'lecturer'. This breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the requirement and the code, and even causes internal inconsistency in the solution (other solution files still reference 'instructor'). This mismatch can confuse students when they try to map the described API to the provided code and may lead to compilation errors or wasted time searching for the expected identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the course teacher across all artifacts. Prefer changing the solution's Course property and initializer parameter from 'lecturer' to 'instructor' (and update all usages) so it matches the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, update problem and template to 'lecturer' everywhere, but keep names consistent across problem_statement.md, Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift, and all usages in Client.swift and Developer.swift.
